conventions.convention: T>0; controls and measurable coefficient data are real almost-everywhere equivalence classes. U_c is nonempty, compact and convex; Q and P are positive semidefinite and rI ≤ R ≤ MI with r>0. Additional constraints enter through a nonempty convex weakly sequentially closed feasible subset.
Numerical stages require pointwise-defined data or chosen representatives and sampling rules; an L-infinity class alone supplies no stage value.
Mesh cells use the half-open representative [t_j,t_{j+1}); the value at T is irrelevant in L2. A refining mesh family means mesh size tends to zero.
The minimization Hamiltonian is H=L+pᵀ(Ax+Bu); the adjoint satisfies -p'=Aᵀp+Q(x-x_d), p(T)=P(x(T)-x_T).
Integral-equation state existence is separated from the almost-everywhere derivative assertion, which assumes Countable Choice.

The pointwise control variational inequality is asserted only when the feasible set is the entire pointwise control set; arbitrary state or terminal constraints retain only the feasible-set integral inequality.

Implicit stages are solved internally. Derivatives must differentiate the actual returned stage map; implicit differentiation requires neighborhood agreement with a nonsingular exact solution branch. Sampled path constraints and embedded RK differences certify neither continuous-path feasibility nor global error.

load_bearing.statement: There is a unique absolutely continuous solution of the stated Volterra equation. Under Countable Choice it satisfies x'=Ax+Bu almost everywhere. The state map is affine into continuous states, and its zero-initial-state linear part is bounded from L2 to the supremum norm.

Defines finite single-shooting, multiple-shooting and internally solved stage-collocation models, with sampled constraints, objective and KKT residuals, actual-map derivatives, and separate construction, stage, IVP, quadrature, mesh and budget statuses.
Assuming Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, DJ(u)[w]=∫(Bᵀp+Ru)ᵀw is bounded linear and J(u+w)-J(u)-DJ(u)[w]=O(‖w‖₂²).

Assume the ultrafilter lemma, Dependent Choice, and Hahn–Banach. For the LQR data, if the feasible-control set is nonempty, convex, and weakly sequentially closed, then J attains its minimum there at a unique control.
For the LQR data, if u_k,u belong to the pointwise admissible set and u_k converges weakly to u in L2, then their states converge uniformly on [0,T].

Under Countable Choice, an absolutely continuous scalar function with derivative zero almost everywhere is constant; a coordinatewise absolutely continuous vector curve whose coordinate derivatives equal a given L1 vector function almost everywhere equals its initial value plus that function's componentwise integral, including a=b.

Under Countable Choice and control-only constraints, uniform-cell averages P_Nu remain pointwise admissible and converge strongly to u in L2. Additional state or terminal constraints require separate preservation or approximation.

concerns.concern: The multiple-shooting/collocation terminal-state domain check is missing. Stage evaluation checks X_{j,0} for j<N, and Transcription modes says 'After every interval map in every mode, check Φ_j∈Ω_x before ... evaluating ... terminal cost, or endpoint constraint'. But the terminal objective is φ(X_{N,0}), and this independent decision variable need not equal Φ_{N-1} at an infeasible candidate. For a one-cell problem with Ω_x=(-1,1), x0=0, f=0, L=0, u=0, and φ(x)=log(1-x²) on Ω_x, choose the multiple-shooting candidate X_{N,0}=2. Every stage/start and computed-endpoint check passes because Φ_0=0, yet the prescribed terminal-cost evaluation is outside its domain. Inputs do not expressly restrict the initial decision vector to terminal-state-domain membership. The procedure needs an explicit check of the actual independent terminal state before terminal cost/constraint queries, or an explicit admissibility restriction covering that variable.

seams_checked.note: The consumer uses g≤0, nonnegative inequality multipliers, the matching Lagrangian and critical-cone SOSC. Its local theorem explicitly assumes a KKT point and the required regularity.
Indirect shooting retains the certified numerical-endpoint derivative interface and the distinction between a computed residual tolerance and an exact BVP or optimality certificate.

Explicit stages use the supplier's ordered tableau recursion. No general order claim is inferred merely from having a tableau; the two-interval exact example assumes consistency and admissible stage times.
The adaptive controller is optional, returns its own finite status, and its embedded difference is consistently denied global-error-certificate status.

The dispatcher supplies strict stored starts, rank checks, finite caps and compatible residual tolerances. A certified gap refers to the resulting stored canonical QP under exact feasibility/stationarity audits; residual candidates remain diagnostic.

Merit calls retain the actual accepted point and full returned QP multipliers. Exact-Hessian quadratic convergence is restricted to full steps with the correct active set, LICQ, strict complementarity, SOSC and a locally Lipschitz active-KKT Jacobian.

The consumer distinguishes the derivative of the actual finite graph from an exact implicit branch. Its use of the weighted gradient-error theorem expressly retains the separate weighted representation, state, adjoint, derivative-data, endpoint and quadrature hypotheses.
